title: Effect of the palatal morphology on the hearing of unilateral cleft-patients - a multicenter pilotstudy
summary:
What is the purpose of the clinical study?
The purpose of this clinical study is to investigate the potential influence of palate shape on hearing ability. Previous studies have already identified a correlation for certain patient groups. This specifically pertains to generally healthy patients with narrow jaws and high palates. Their hearing ability was found to be worse than that of patients with a normal palate shape.
The ongoing study aims to determine whether this correlation also exists for patients with cleft lip and palate. To clarify the relationship, patients without cleft malformations will also be included in the study as a control group.

How does it work?
This clinical study is being conducted at multiple locations with a total of approximately 300 participants. Participation in this clinical study is expected to take about 1 hour and will occur on a single day.

The following measures will be carried out solely for study purposes:
a) Assessment of health status
b) Ear inspection
c) Eardrum mobility test (tympanometry)
d) Hearing test (audiometry)
e) Digital impression of the upper jaw
conditions: Cleft hard and soft palate with unilateral cleft lip
